rules.quote: Don’t add full stops to the ends of headings, page headers, footers or captions.
rules.violation_condition: A heading, page header, footer or caption ends with a full stop.
when: Applies to headings, page headers, footers and captions.
rules.why: G-2: the four locations are conditions for the same terminal-full-stop check.

rules.quote: Don’t use a semicolon at the end of each item in a bullet list.
rules.violation_condition: A bullet-list item has a semicolon as its terminal punctuation.
when: Applies to bullet lists.
rules.why: G-1: this is a specific child check under the minimal-punctuation introduction.

rules.quote: Unless each item is a full sentence or the last item in a list, don’t use a full stop for items in bullet lists.
rules.violation_condition: A bullet-list item ends with a full stop even though it is neither a full sentence nor the last item.
when: Applies to bullet-list items.
A full stop is permitted for a full-sentence item.
A full stop is permitted for the last item.
rules.why: G-2/G-3: sentence completeness and final-item position are exceptions to one check, not separate rules.

rules.quote: Don’t use full stops between letters in an acronym or initialism.
rules.violation_condition: An acronym or initialism contains full stops between its letters.
when: Applies to acronyms and initialisms.
Does not prohibit sentence-ending punctuation after an acronym or initialism.
rules.why: G-1: internal full stops in shortened forms are a distinct, actionable child check.

rules.quote: Don’t use a full stop at the end of most abbreviations.
rules.specification: The page does not identify the exceptions implied by ‘most abbreviations’. An exception list is needed before this check can reliably distinguish permitted and prohibited abbreviation punctuation.
rules.violation_condition: An abbreviation has an abbreviation-marking full stop at its end and is not among the exceptions.
when: Applies to abbreviation punctuation, not a full stop serving to end the sentence.
Some abbreviations are excepted, but this page does not identify them.
rules.why: G-2: the unspecified exceptions belong to this check; they must not be invented.

rules.quote: Include a single space after a punctuation mark at the end of a sentence.
rules.violation_condition: Within a paragraph, a sentence-ending punctuation mark is immediately followed by the next sentence without an intervening space.
when: Applies between successive sentences in running text.
Runs of two or more spaces are handled by the separate repeated-space check.
rules.why: The missing-space and repeated-space checks are partitioned so that the same gap is not flagged twice.

rules.violation_condition: Running text contains a run of two or more spaces.
rules.why: G-5: retain the observable repeated-space prohibition, not the accompanying instruction to check and delete.

when: Applies to symbols of units of measurement.
Capitals are permitted when their use is standardised or specified in regulations.
rules.why: G-2/G-3: standardisation and regulations are alternative conditions permitting capitals, not separate rules.

anchor.quote: Use capitals when an official title precedes the name of the office holder.

covers.prefix: the name of the office holder.
covers.quote: This includes titles for executives specified in legislation.

examples.note: The official title precedes the named office holder.

parts.quote: Chief Defence Scientist Tanya Monro presented the award ...

tags.violation_condition: An official title immediately before the office holder’s name lacks the required capitals.

when: Applies when an official title precedes the office holder’s name.
Includes executive titles specified in legislation.
rules.why: G-2/E-2: legislative executive titles are an included case; the Write this example tests this title-before-name rule.

anchor.quote: In these cases, use the form of the name as it is written in the legislation.

covers.quote: Legal documents often use initial capitals to show terms with a defined meaning (such as ‘Department’, ‘Schedule’, ‘Vendor’ and ‘Recipient’).
covers.suffix: In these cases, use the form of

tags.violation_condition: A name or term with a defined meaning in legislation is written in a different form, including different capitalisation, from the legislative form.

when: Applies in legal documents using names or terms with defined legislative meanings.
rules.why: G-4: the body instruction states the check; the preceding sentence establishes its legal-defined-term context.
